cues.en: A while ago I made a video on The US electrical system.
cues.zh: 之前我做过一期关于美国电力系统的视频。

cues.en: It was a basic overview designed principally to get those of you in two forty lands to shut...
cues.zh: 那是个基础概览，主要目的是让来自 240 伏国家的各位别再……

cues.en: To understand that we are also a two forty land. But since we use split phase power, most of our circuits operate at half that voltage and the full 240 volts potential is generally limited to high power devices on dedicated circuits.
cues.zh: 明白我们其实也是 240 伏国家。只不过我们用的是分相供电，所以大多数电路都跑在一半的电压上，完整的 240 伏电压一般只用于专线供电的大功率设备。

cues.en: Using split phase power has some real advantages particularly when it comes to safety. And on that note, at the end I'm gonna add some clarifying words there because in the time since that video I discovered an interesting language quirk regarding that discussion.
cues.zh: 用分相供电确实有不少好处，尤其是在安全方面。说到这儿，结尾我还要补充几句澄清的话，因为那期视频之后我发现，那部分讨论里有个挺有意思的语言习惯问题。

cues.en: But anyway, this video isn't gonna defend our electrical system. In fact, it's about perhaps the worst part of it.
cues.zh: 但总之，这个视频不是要替我们的电气系统辩护。实际上，它讲的是其中也许最糟糕的部分。

cues.en: And no, it's not just our terrible fully metal plug design or completely unshielded receptacles,
cues.zh: 不，问题也不只是我们糟糕的全金属插头设计，或完全没有防护的插座，

cues.en: although for what it's worth tamper resistant receptacles are now available and usually required in new construction.
cues.zh: 不过话说回来，防误触插座现在已经有了，而且新建建筑通常要求安装。

cues.en: But, anyway, this problem has actually nothing to do with a building's wiring or the receptacles or the plugs.
cues.zh: 但总之，这个问题其实跟建筑的布线、插座或插头都没有关系。

cues.en: Instead,
cues.zh: 相反，

cues.en: it's that these exist.
cues.zh: 而在于这些东西的存在。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 还有

cues.en: these.
cues.zh: 这些。

cues.en: And especially
cues.zh: 尤其是

cues.en: these.
cues.zh: 这些。

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 现在，

cues.en: there's nothing wrong with extension cords or power strips themselves,
cues.zh: 延长线或插线板本身没有问题，

cues.en: it's just how they're implemented which is the issue. Here's a silly fact to preview the problem at hand. A strand of Christmas lights is a safer extension cord than most extension cords.
cues.zh: 问题只在于它们是怎么实现的。先讲个离谱的事实，来预览一下眼前的问题：一串圣诞彩灯作为延长线，比大多数延长线更安全。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 是啊。

cues.en: I'll explain why in a bit but first we need to address a common misconception.
cues.zh: 稍后我会解释原因，但首先得澄清一个常见误解。

cues.en: Circuit breakers.
cues.zh: 断路器。

cues.en: What are they for?
cues.zh: 它们是干什么用的？

cues.en: Well, you might think that they're there to protect you and your stuff.
cues.zh: 你可能会以为，它们是为了保护你和你的财物。

cues.en: This belief is pretty understandable.
cues.zh: 这种想法很容易理解。

cues.en: After all, one of the most common ways they get tripped is when one of your electrical stuffs has a bad time.
cues.zh: 毕竟，它们最常见的跳闸原因之一，就是你的某个电器出了故障。

cues.en: And since they cut the power to a given circuit when they do their thing, well it stands to reason that they also help prevent electric shock.
cues.zh: 而且，既然它们动作时会切断特定电路的电源，那按理说，它们也有助于防止触电。

cues.en: But a breaker like these does no such thing. It couldn't care less about your stuff and quite frankly it doesn't care about you either.
cues.zh: 但像这样的断路器并不做这种事。它根本不在乎你的财物，说实话，也不在乎你。

cues.en: Of course there is some nuance here with the advent of arc fault circuit interrupters,
cues.zh: 当然，随着电弧故障断路器的出现，这里有些细节要注意，

cues.en: and while we usually only put shock protection devices at the receptacle in locations where hands can be wet, breakers with integrated residual current devices are
cues.zh: 虽然我们通常只在手可能弄湿的场所把防触电装置装在插座处，但带集成剩余电流装置的断路器也

cues.en: available.
cues.zh: 有售。

cues.en: I actually made a video about that tech if you wanna check it out. It's pretty interesting.
cues.zh: 其实我做过一期关于这项技术的视频，感兴趣可以看看。挺有意思的。

cues.en: But anyway, since AFCI breakers have only somewhat recently been mandated by code and GFCI
cues.zh: 不过话说回来，AFCI 断路器直到最近才被规范强制要求，而 GFCI

cues.en: breakers are frankly quite rare here, you're gonna find lots of electrical panels like this one filled with nothing but bog standard breakers.
cues.zh: 断路器说实话在这里相当少见，所以你会发现很多像这样的配电箱，里面清一色都是普通标准断路器。

cues.en: And these have one job and one job only. To protect the conductors in your walls.
cues.zh: 它们只有一个职责，而且仅此一个：保护墙内的导线。

cues.en: That's it. They frankly do not care what happens when the electricity leaves the wall, they just want to know that you're not overloading the wiring coming out of them. They will stand idly by as you get zapped or as your television has a meltdown and will only intervene once the current going through them exceeds their rating.
cues.zh: 就是这样。坦白说，它们不在乎电离开墙后发生什么，只想知道你没有让从它们引出的线路过载。你被电到、或者电视烧坏时，它们会袖手旁观；只有当通过它们的电流超过额定值，它们才会介入。

cues.en: Circuit breakers like these are overcurrent
cues.zh: 像这样的断路器是过流

cues.en: protection devices for a structure's electrical system,
cues.zh: 保护装置，用于建筑的电气系统，

cues.en: and nothing more.
cues.zh: 仅此而已。

cues.en: They reduce the risk of electrical fires occurring due to an overheating conductor igniting a wall stud or whatever but that's about the only thing they can do.
cues.zh: 它们能降低因导体过热引燃墙骨之类东西而导致电气火灾的风险，但这差不多就是它们唯一能做的事。

cues.en: Now that is very important.
cues.zh: 这一点非常重要。

cues.en: A given conductor,
cues.zh: 给定的一根导体，

cues.en: so a wire, can only carry so much current before its own electrical resistance becomes significant and it begins to heat up.
cues.zh: 也就是电线，只能承载有限的电流；超过后自身电阻会变得显著，并开始发热。

cues.en: And that's bad.
cues.zh: 这很糟糕。

cues.en: Imagine you had a coffee maker and a microwave
cues.zh: 想象一下，你有一台咖啡机和一台微波炉

cues.en: and why not also a toaster all connected to the same circuit.
cues.zh: 为什么不再加一台烤面包机，全都接在同一条电路上。

cues.en: This can be easier to accomplish than you might think as many adjacent outlets are simply daisy chained and share the same wires in the walls. Though, in fairness, kitchens are usually designed more smartly to avoid this.
cues.zh: 这可能比你想象的更容易发生，因为许多相邻插座只是菊花链式连接，共用墙里的同一组电线。不过公平地说，厨房通常设计得更聪明，会避免这种情况。

cues.en: Now, on a 15 amp 120 volt circuit, eighteen
cues.zh: 现在，在 15 安培 120 伏特的电路上，一千八百

cues.en: seventy five watts is the maximum that can be safely drawn, and in fact that number is really only good for non continuous loads.
cues.zh: 七十五瓦是能安全取用的最大值，而且实际上，这个数字只适用于非连续负载。

cues.en: Devices which draw a load continuously
cues.zh: 持续带载的电器

cues.en: are limited to 80% of a circuit's capacity.
cues.zh: 被限制在电路容量的 80%。

cues.en: Let's say the toaster uses seven fifty watts, and we'll imagine the coffee maker is a thousand.
cues.zh: 假设烤面包机用 750 瓦，再假定咖啡机是 1000 瓦。

cues.en: Making some toast while brewing coffee is really close to the limit.
cues.zh: 一边烤吐司一边煮咖啡，就已经非常接近上限了。

cues.en: And if you decide to microwave some bacon while that's going on,
cues.zh: 而如果你在这一切进行时再用微波炉热些培根，

cues.en: now you could easily be more than a kilowatt over.
cues.zh: 那很容易就会超出 1 千瓦以上。

cues.en: That is going to cause the wiring coming from the breaker panel up to wherever you are to get pretty hot particularly where splices and other connections have been made.
cues.zh: 这会导致从断路器面板一路到你所在位置的布线变得相当热，尤其是在接线和其他连接处。

cues.en: Because there tends to be flammable material in or near walls,
cues.zh: 因为墙内或墙附近往往有易燃材料，

cues.en: this is very bad. And that's why these are here. They help prevent that. If you pull more power than the wires can safely carry, the breaker will trip and kill the circuit.
cues.zh: 这非常糟糕。这就是它们存在的原因。它们有助于防止这种情况。如果你用的电功率超过电线能安全承载的范围，断路器就会跳闸，切断电路。

cues.en: How do circuit breakers work?
cues.zh: 断路器是如何工作的？

cues.en: Well, we'll save that for later, and then we'll get into the stuff like arc fault protection and other goodies.
cues.zh: 这个我们留到后面再讲，然后会聊聊电弧故障保护之类的内容和其他好东西。

cues.en: I'll try to remember to come back here and put a card for that video but I have a bad track record there.
cues.zh: 我会尽量记得回到这里，给那个视频加张卡片，但在这方面我以往记录很差。

cues.en: Anyway,
cues.zh: 总之，

cues.en: here's the problem. This will do a fantastic job of making sure the wiring in your walls doesn't get overloaded.
cues.zh: 问题在这里。这能很好地确保你墙内的布线不会过载。

cues.en: But once you're outside of the wall,
cues.zh: 但一旦出了墙，

cues.en: this won't help you.
cues.zh: 这就不管用了。

cues.en: And since we like to cut costs wherever possible so we can sell cheap stuff,
cues.zh: 而且我们总想尽可能削减成本，好卖便宜货，

cues.en: you will find
cues.zh: 你会发现

cues.en: countless extension cords and power strips which cannot safely handle the capacity of the circuits they're plugged into.
cues.zh: 无数延长线和插线板无法安全承受它们所插入电路的容量。

cues.en: Let's talk about wire gauge.
cues.zh: 我们来聊聊线规。

cues.en: The amount of current a given conductor can carry safely depends on what it's made from as well as its total cross sectional area. And also length.
cues.zh: 给定导体能安全承载的电流大小，取决于它的材质以及总横截面积。还有长度。

cues.en: There's some nuance with stranded versus solid wire and with really weird stuff like the skin effect but we're not going there. Now, I'm going to be talking in the American wire gauge. I know not everyone uses that. Here's a chart for those that want it. But the main point is that a given gauge of wire has a given maximum current it can carry
cues.zh: 多股线和单股实心线之间有些细微差别，还有像集肤效应这种很特殊的情况，但我们不展开。现在我会用美国线规来讲。我知道不是所有人都用它。需要的话这里有一张图表。但重点是，特定线规的导线能承载的最大电流是固定的

cues.en: before it becomes a problem.
cues.zh: 超过就会出问题。

cues.en: Now, crash course. The smaller the number, the thicker the wire. 14 gauge wire can carry less current than 12 gauge wire. 12 gauge is thicker than 14 gauge which is thicker than 16 gauge, and so on.
cues.zh: 快速入门：数字越小，电线越粗。14 号电线能承载的电流比 12 号电线小。12 号比 14 号粗，14 号又比 16 号粗，以此类推。

cues.en: It's confusing but are you really surprised?
cues.zh: 这确实让人困惑，但你真会意外吗？

cues.en: Except for circuits which handle things like water heaters, dryers, stoves, etc,
cues.zh: 除了热水器、烘干机、炉灶等设备所用的电路外，

cues.en: you're generally going to have a mix of 15 amp and 20 amp circuits in an American home.
cues.zh: 美国家庭通常会混合使用 15 安和 20 安电路。

cues.en: It has become pretty common these days to run 20 amp circuits for most receptacles and reserve 15 amps for lighting circuits,
cues.zh: 如今很常见的是，大多数插座用 20 安培电路，照明电路则留 15 安培，

cues.en: but not always.
cues.zh: 但也不总是这样。

cues.en: Now, it shouldn't surprise you that 20 amp circuits need thicker wires than 15 amp circuits.
cues.zh: 所以，20 安培电路需要比 15 安培电路更粗的电线，这应该不意外。

cues.en: In runs with typical lengths, 15 amp circuits will use 14 gauge wire and 20 amp circuits use 12 gauge wire.
cues.zh: 在典型长度的布线中，15 安培电路用 14 号线规电线，20 安培电路用 12 号线规电线。

cues.en: This is what that wiring looks like in homes all across the country. With some particular caveats, we don't need to get into that. Discuss in the comments, it boosts engagement. Anyway, this is called THHN
cues.zh: 全国各地的家庭里，这种布线看起来就是这样。有些特殊例外，我们不必深入。评论区聊聊吧，能提升互动。总之，这叫作 THHN

cues.en: wiring, short for thermoplastic
cues.zh: 电线，是 thermoplastic 的缩写

cues.en: high heat resistant nylon coated
cues.zh: 耐高温尼龙涂层

cues.zh: 作弊线。但通常它就叫 Romex，Romex 之于家庭布线，就像 Kleenex 之于面巾纸。

cues.en: Conveniently it's been color coded for many years now. 14 gauge wiring has white sheathing,
cues.zh: 很方便的是，这种线多年来一直用颜色区分。14 号线规的电线带白色护套，

cues.en: and 12 gauge wiring has yellow sheathing. It helps you know at a glance which is which, and yellow wires will be for 20 amp circuits, white wires for 15.
cues.zh: 12 号线规的电线带黄色护套。这样一眼就能分清；黄线用于 20 安培电路，白线用于 15 安培。

cues.en: Oddly, there is also orange for 10 gauge wire, good for up to 30 amps depending on the length of the run, but then after that the color coding goes out the window. Anyway,
cues.zh: 奇怪的是，10 号线规还有橙色，视走线长度最高可用于 30 安培，但再往上颜色编码就不管用了。总之，

cues.en: the circuit breakers?
cues.zh: 断路器呢？

cues.en: They're protecting
cues.zh: 它们保护着

cues.en: this stuff.
cues.zh: 这些东西。

cues.en: They're making sure you don't put too much current through these wires.
cues.zh: 它们确保你不会让太多电流通过这些电线。

cues.en: But these wires are inside your walls.
cues.zh: 但这些电线是埋在墙里的。

cues.en: This one goes on the outside.
cues.zh: 而这一根是走在外面的。

cues.en: And the problem is that this cannot handle the amount of current that the wires in the walls can especially on 20 amp circuits.
cues.zh: 问题在于，它承受不了墙内电线所能承受的电流量，尤其是在 20 安培的电路上。

cues.en: But your circuit breakers don't know that.
cues.zh: 但你的断路器并不知道这一点。

cues.en: Now this doesn't have to be a problem. One of the best features of The UK's electrical system is that the plugs have fuses in them.
cues.zh: 这倒不一定是个问题。英国电气系统最好的特点之一，就是插头里自带保险丝。

cues.en: Now the reason for that is kinda weird.
cues.zh: 原因还挺奇怪的。

cues.en: Ring circuits.
cues.zh: 环形电路。

cues.en: What were you thinking? But anyway, the lasting benefit there is that you could provide overcurrent protection
cues.zh: 你们当时怎么想的？不过不管怎样，它长久的好处是能在墙的另一侧提供过流保护

cues.en: on the other side of the wall, allowing you to safely use smaller wiring that's sized according to the device's needs.
cues.zh: 让你可以安全地使用更细的导线，线径按设备需求来定。

cues.en: If you put in a seven amp fuse, well then that fuse will blow before the wire gets overloaded. Simple.
cues.zh: 如果你装个七安的保险丝，那在线路过载之前保险丝就先熔断了。就这么简单。

cues.zh: 这根延长线用的是 16 AWG 导线，额定功率只有 16

cues.zh: 25 瓦，或 13 安培。然而，

cues.zh: 就算接上技术上允许的 12 安培负载，也会让这根线热得令人不安

cues.en: warm. But on any otherwise unloaded circuit you can still pull at least another three amps through here without the breaker tripping.
cues.zh: 发热。但在原本空载的电路上，你还能再从这里抽取至少 3 安培，而断路器不会跳闸。

cues.en: As far as it's concerned, well there's nothing wrong. 15 amps are on the wires in the walls, which is okay.

cues.en: That's ideally how everything should work. But on a 20 amp circuit you can now severely overload this without the circuit breaker carrying.
cues.zh: 理想情况下一切都该这样工作。但在20安培电路上，你现在可以让它严重过载，而断路器却不会动作。

cues.en: And of course that problem still applies to a cord like this which can handle even less.

cues.en: The outlets in this room are on the 20 amp circuit. So, I could plug a space heater into this. And also another one on medium.
cues.zh: 这个房间的插座接在20安培电路上。所以，我可以把一台电暖器插到这里。再插另一台，开到中档。

cues.en: That is now 20 amps going through a cord which is only rated for 13.

cues.en: It's a very dangerous situation especially if the cord is near anything flammable like, oh I don't know, curtains, carpet, a sofa,
cues.zh: 这非常危险，尤其当电线靠近任何易燃物时，比如——呃，谁知道呢——窗帘、地毯、沙发，

cues.en: Complicating things further is that you don't necessarily even know what circuits are 20 amps and which ones aren't.

cues.zh: 就是这里随处可见的普通插座。而这个是NEMA 5-20R插座。

cues.en: You will only find these on 20 amp circuits. The neutral pin is t shaped to accommodate a NEMA five twenty plug which looks like this. You basically never see this plug outside of commercial settings as it's reserved for devices which actually need more than 15 amps to operate.
cues.zh: 这种插座只出现在20安培电路上。它的中性线插孔是T形的，用来兼容长这样的NEMA 5-20插头。这种插头基本只在商业场所出现，因为它是专门留给真正需要超过15安培才能运行的设备的。

cues.en: But you aren't always required to use NEMA five twenty R receptacles on 20 amp circuits.
cues.zh: 但你不一定必须在 20 安培电路上使用 NEMA 5-20R 插座。

cues.zh: 事实上，如果我没理解错的话，

cues.zh: 而由于这里双联插座是常态，

cues.en: So anyway, you usually can't tell by looking at an outlet if it's a 15 or 20 amp circuit, and we don't put protection on things like extension cords so really it's just a mess. It's terrible.
cues.zh: 所以不管怎样，你通常无法光看插座就判断它是 15 安培还是 20 安培电路，而且我们不会给延长线之类的东西加保护，所以这真是一团糟。太糟了。

The report even says 50% of these fires are of unclassified cause so frankly I don't know how useful this study is for this particular discussion.

cues.zh: 最后，来说说我在开头提到的那个语言上的古怪之处。这和“更安全”这个词有关。

cues.en: See, here's what I said in that original video.
cues.zh: 是这样的，以下是我在最初那期视频里说的。

cues.en: In any given scenario where one is receiving an electric shock,
cues.zh: 在任何特定场景下，当一个人正在遭受电击时，

cues.en: a lower voltage is safer than a higher one when all other factors are the same.
cues.zh: 在所有其他因素都相同的情况下，较低的电压比更高的电压更安全。

cues.en: Therefore, 120
volts could, and I would say should,
cues.zh: 伏可以说，而且我认为应该说，

cues.en: be considered safer than 240
cues.zh: 被认为比240

cues.en: volts.
cues.zh: 伏更安全。

cues.en: Now, here's where things get wonky. I use the word safer synonymously
cues.zh: 那么，问题就出在这里。我把“更安全”这个词当作

cues.en: with less dangerous.
cues.zh: “危险更小”的同义词来使用。

cues.en: Just as how I think extension cords would be safer if they had fuses,
cues.zh: 就像我认为延长线如果装了保险丝会更安全，

cues.en: but that doesn't necessarily mean that they would be 100%
cues.zh: 但这并不一定意味着它们会 100%

cues.en: safe.
cues.zh: 安全。

cues.en: But I found that a lot of people interpret the word safer
cues.zh: 但我发现很多人把“更安全”这个词理解为

cues.en: as implying some amount of baseline safety.
cues.zh: 暗示存在某种基础安全水平。

cues.en: I found out because people told me. And the thing is, that's just not at all how that word functions for me.
cues.zh: 我是因为别人告诉我才发现的。问题是，这个词对我来说根本不是这么用的。

cues.en: I use it literally as a stand in for less dangerous or perhaps less risky.
cues.zh: 我只是把它当作“没那么危险”或“风险可能更低”的替代说法。

cues.en: Like how driving a 100 miles an hour with your headlights on is safer
cues.zh: 就像开着车前灯、以每小时100英里的速度行驶会更安全

cues.en: than driving the same speed in the dark.
cues.zh: 比在黑暗中以同样的速度行驶更安全。

cues.en: That statement doesn't suggest to me that driving a 100 miles an hour is a safe activity.
cues.zh: 这句话在我看来，并不意味着时速100英里是项安全的活动。

cues.en: It's just safer than doing a 100 by moonlight.
cues.zh: 它只是比在月光下开100英里更安全而已。

cues.en: To me, safer is always a comparator alone and doesn't bring its own implication of any safety.
cues.zh: 对我来说，“更安全”永远只是个比较词，本身并不暗示任何安全性。

cues.en: So,
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: yeah, I actually was genuinely delighted to hear this explanation because I was starting to lose my mind thinking Ohm's Law was a trick or something.
cues.zh: 是的，听到这个解释我真的很高兴，因为我之前都快想疯了，还以为欧姆定律是个套路什么的。

cues.en: And I am absolutely
cues.zh: 而且我完全

cues.en: in agreement that the shock mitigation efforts in 240 volt countries are by and large much better than ours.
cues.zh: 同意，240 伏国家的防触电措施总体上比我们好得多。

cues.en: It's stupidly easy to get a shock here. Seriously, just hold the plug wrong and you'll get a tingle. So I'm not saying that our electrical system
cues.zh: 在这里触电简直容易得离谱。说真的，插头拿错一下，你就会被电得麻一下。所以我不是说我们的电气系统

cues.en: is safer than your electrical system because it's undeniably not.
cues.zh: 比你们的更安全，因为不可否认，它确实不是。

cues.en: But I am saying that because the voltage is lower, electric shocks are less likely to be fatal over here, and that's why our efforts to prevent them are half assed.
cues.zh: 但我是说，因为电压更低，这里的电击不太容易致命，所以我们在防触电上才这么敷衍了事。

cues.en: The voltage itself is safer, as in less dangerous.
cues.zh: 电压本身更安全，也就是没那么危险。

cues.en: The electrical system as a whole though, sure isn't.
cues.zh: 不过整个电气系统嘛，绝对不算安全。

cues.en: Anyway, toodles.
cues.zh: 总之，拜拜啦。

cues.en: It couldn't care less about you and... Shoot.
cues.zh: 它才不管你呢，而且……糟了。

cues.en: Circuit breakers like these are over... Well,
cues.zh: 像这样的断路器太……好吧，

cues.en: that was nice. Igniting a wall stud or whatever. But that's a...
cues.zh: 那可真不错。把墙骨柱点着了还是怎么着。不过那是个……

cues.en: Would you please stop doing that? This is a NEMA five twenty r receptacle.
cues.zh: 你能不能别这样了？这是 NEMA 5-20R 插座。

cues.en: I'm holding it upside down.
cues.zh: 我把它拿反了。

cues.en: You can tell that I start every shoot with everything I need.
cues.zh: 看得出来，我每次拍摄一开始就备齐了所有需要的东西。

cues.en: Right?
cues.zh: 对吧？

cues.en: I don't think it's awful by any means, and it does continue to get... And
cues.zh: 我完全不觉得它糟糕，而且它确实还在继续变……而且

cues.en: especially
cues.zh: 尤其是

cues.en: with these.
cues.zh: 有了这些。

cues.en: And I only got the one.
cues.zh: 而且我只拿到了一个。

cues.en: Oh, well.
cues.zh: 哦，好吧。
